agree.reason: The judge gets a clear need (300 turned away, 80 cases per attorney) and a funded ask, but with no baseline for the 58%, no estimate of how many more tenants a third lawyer would serve, and an unclear answer on whether the hire only replaces the departing attorney, a skeptical scorer will probably mark it middling.

honest.reason: The figures are accurate (65/78 is 83%), but saying the position "does not depend on" the county renewal overstates things, since the $13,000 a year comes from a general budget that leans on that $60,000 contract.

works_the_facts.reason: The only derived figure is the 83% cost share; the draft never works out that the clinic reached about 14% of filings, what the 300 turnaways mean as a share of demand, roughly how many added cases a third attorney at about 80 cases would cover, or what the June departure does to capacity.

right_comparison.reason: The no-grant scenario is never spelled out (one attorney left after June, even more tenants turned away), and the 58% appears with no note that there is no figure for tenants without a lawyer, so the reader can't judge it.

qualification.reason: The October renewal is mentioned and then waved away instead of qualified, there's no consequence if it lapses, and the checkable commitments (six-month reports, a request for clerk comparison data starting in January) are dropped or weakened to annual reports.

objections.reason: The judge's likely questions (is this a third attorney or just a replacement, what does 58% mean without a baseline, how quickly can someone be hired given the 5-month last search and the June departure) go unanswered, even though the facts about training and the clerk data were available to answer them.
